correctness.rationale: Disk and height-separation density from product uniform sampling are normalized. Fixed-volume moment is pointwise strictly log-convex in log aspect ratio and coercive, guaranteeing a unique optimizer for each p>0. Exact p=2 and p=4 polynomial checks give the claimed roots. Endpoint t→2 and u→1 densities give a uniform differentiable boundary-Laplace expansion p^-9/2 with prefactor sqrt(2/pi)(4+q^2)^(9/2)/q^4; differentiating proves the 9sqrt(2)/(4p) term. Independent numerical quadrature and direct 350000-pair simulation passed; they are not substituted for proof.

value.rationale: The fixed-volume solid-cylinder random-distance energy is a natural geometric shape functional. Its complete p>0 unique-optimum theorem is stronger than an isolated second-moment calculation. The exact mismatch between q2 and q4, convergence to the diameter-optimal ratio, and sharp high-power 9sqrt(2)/(4p) displacement expose nontrivial endpoint pair-geometry with an explicit p^-9/2 Laplace mechanism; results offer testable benchmarks and a structural template for product-body optimization.
